gen-gf-warnes-gf-mozilla-text: Mozilla Text has tall, sturdy-looking lowercase with flared terminals. Warnes is the showman here, stretched out with ink strokes that taper away before they touch, while the sans just gets on with the text.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-nata-sans: Expressive Warnes stretches out, its ink strokes tapering away before they touch. Nata Sans holds the line with a large central band and open-mouthed curves, drawn with technical-pen steadiness, so one shouts and the other keeps time.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-noto-sans-avestan: Warnes stretches out wide, every tail and terminal matching the stems in thickness. Noto Sans Avestan, a plain sans with open curve tips and a pronounced x-height, supplies the pull: loud above, plain below.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-noto-sans-bamum: Loud and stretched, Warnes draws ink strokes that taper out before touching, with essentially no stroke contrast. Noto Sans Bamum, a plain sans with big open counters in every small letter, turns that shout into a conversation.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-noto-sans-batak: Noto Sans Batak stands tall, its x-height like a stubby carpenter's pencil stroke. Long paragraphs would read friendly and steady, its wide e never looking squeezed, while Warnes keeps its stretched tracking for the heading.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-noto-sans-bengali: Contemporary Noto Sans Bengali, a sans-serif body, keeps its capitals barely taller than lowercase and its letter mouths distinctly open. Warnes, all hollow glass-tube lettering, glows above while the body stays put.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-noto-sans-bhaiksuki: Line width never changes between the curves and straights of Warnes, whose strokes taper away before touching. Noto Sans Bhaiksuki is the one to read, with swollen lowercase and open apertures that never close up.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-noto-sans-brahmi: Noto Sans Brahmi reads crisp and open, its mean line set high and every curved letter left open-ended. Page after page it would feel light, while Warnes sits stretched above.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-noto-sans-cham: Noto Sans Cham has tall rounded lowercase and a generous opening in every c. Noto Sans Cham would read smoothly for pages on end, leaving the wire-bent look of Warnes to the heading.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-noto-sans-coptic: Stretched and single-stroked, Warnes keeps one width in every glyph, with ink strokes that taper out before touching. Noto Sans Coptic, a sans-serif with a dominant middle zone and uncrowded s and c, gives it somewhere to rest.
